two-sided.A: The lower yellow's side spur is reduced without trimming the red left or yellow right out of the comparison; all three remain high. Some peripheral red supports still conflict.
two-sided.B: The red left and yellow right are represented and the lower yellow is separated. Added supports at lower/outer edges need review; exclusive pixels do not prove separate beads.
two-sided.C: The lower yellow spur is removed but a notch replaces it. Left red remains high; right yellow becomes a partial, unresolved support. Strict paths lose useful shaded material.

duplicate.A: Upper black reflection passes; lower stays unresolved rather than becoming high. The red to the right loses high status because another cue overlaps it.
duplicate.B: Upper black and the red right pass; lower reflection stays unresolved. Competition separates masks but supplies no primary/secondary interpretation.
duplicate.C: Upper black has a 40-pixel reflection/collar support. Lower is an 8-pixel secondary hypothesis linked to it; red right passes. The second secondary link in this crop is unverified.

abstention.A: The reviewed yellow becomes one compact 355-pixel high support; the old excursion toward the upper-left patch is cut. Adjacent yellows still have unresolved shared material.
abstention.B: The reviewed yellow becomes a bounded 399-pixel high support. Neighboring seeds have separate owners, but some partitions elsewhere in the crop can split one body.
abstention.C: The reviewed yellow is trimmed to 236 pixels and remains unresolved. Native brightness stopping cuts irregular crescents; this is an informative failure, not a recommended yellow outline.

auto-red.A: The central crossing red remains compact. The yellow at its left has multiple conflicting cues and is withheld, reducing accepted two-sided coverage.
auto-red.B: Central red is retained, but the left yellow is visibly split into several high supports (1/4/10). The extra near count includes over-segmentation.
auto-red.C: Central red stays high with small native notches. Left yellow conflicts remain unresolved; brightness paths do not settle multiple cue ownership.

auto-yellow.A: The central crossing yellow is retained; multiple cues on yellows to the right are questioned. Good shape alone does not settle identity.
auto-yellow.B: More near supports pass, but the right yellow is divided into high pieces (2/12), with another split below. These cannot be counted as extra recovered bodies.
auto-yellow.C: The selected central yellow survives; right-side yellow fragments can still pass separately. Ray stopping is not a complete duplicate solution.

auto-black.A: The selected near-line black reflection stays compact. Neighboring yellow conflicts reduce coverage; no full black silhouette is inferred.
auto-black.B: The selected black passes, but the left yellow/highlight is divided among cues. Wider accepted coverage needs a distinct-body check.
auto-black.C: The selected black is represented by compact reflection plus collar; colored paths make notches and leave nearby yellow alternatives unresolved.

auto-opposite.A: The opposing central yellow/red supports remain represented without forcing their centroids onto the line. Lower-right same-color cues remain ambiguous.
auto-opposite.B: Central flanking supports survive and more neighbors pass. Upper/lower edge partitions remain possible duplicate or background features.
auto-opposite.C: The crossing pair is retained, but adjacent yellow paths cut deep notches and one lower red is withheld. High two-sided coverage is weaker.

auto-three.A: The center crossing yellow and nearby black reflections survive. Left yellow alternatives remain unresolved; three visible candidates are not certified as three owned bodies.
auto-three.B: Several neighbors on both sides pass, including left yellows. Some apparent gains reflect resolving overlaps by partition, which still needs identity evidence.
auto-three.C: The central yellow breaks into a partial unresolved support, losing an important crossing candidate. Compact black reflections remain, but the whole colored rule is unsuitable here.
